episodes.name: The Comfort of Avoiding: The Hidden Patterns That Keep Us Stuck
episodes.description:
Avoidance isn’t laziness it is protection.

In this episode, I explore avoidance not as laziness but as protection. The subtle ways we distance ourselves from hard conversations, from uncomfortable emotions, from risks that might expose us.

I share how I’ve mistaken withdrawal for strength, intellectualizing for clarity, perfectionism for standards. How I’ve avoided anger. Avoided love. Avoided being seen before I felt ready.

Avoidance works. That’s the problem. It gives relief. It buys time. It keeps us intact.

.This conversation isn’t about shame. It’s about awareness. About naming the pattern.

About choosing discomfort in small, intentional doses.

What are you Avoiding?

Host: JD Ferrell

Produced by: JD Ferrell

Presented by the Modern Podcast Network and themodernHQ.com

Follow us on Instagram: @ThemoderntherapistJD & @theModernHQ

episodes.name: What Collective Radical Healing Looks Like
episodes.description:
In this episode of A Modern Man, JD Ferrell explores Collective Radical Healing—moving beyond survival and symptom management toward thriving, critical consciousness, and shared liberation. He breaks down the difference between coping and healing, unpacks the five anchors of radical healing, and examines how community, activism, grief, and resistance shape psychological well-being. This episode invites listeners to reflect on how individualism, denial, and disconnection keep us stuck—and what becomes possible when healing is rooted in collective change.

episodes.name: From the Village, To Girl Dad, Through Covid with Scott DeRosa
episodes.description:
On this episode of A Modern Man Podcast, I am joined by my friend Scott Derosa. Scott and I met playing volleyball this fall. He talks about his struggles growing up with a father of addiction in the panhandle of West Texas. He did not come from a diverse community, but the village that raised him taught him to love his neighbor regardless of who they are and what they look like. He then left the small town with big-city dreams just outside of Houston. He spent a few years there until he met his eventual wife. This led him to be a girl dad to 3 incredible young girls at such a young age. He made the commitment and moved to Oklahoma City in 2008, and he has been here ever since. After a decade of marriage, covid came. He thought he was changing careers and inevitably leaving Oklahoma, but the pandemic changed that. He was lucky enough to stay at his job for a few months longer than expected, but after that, he was unsure of his future. All he knows for sure is that he wants to be honest and respectful of everyone’s struggle and he understands we all need help sometimes.

episodes.name: EP 38 | Why I Pray Every Morning (And How It Rewires My Brain)
episodes.description:
In this episode, Jenna Marilyn talks about prayer and why it doesn’t have to belong to religion to be powerful. She shares the exact structure she says every morning and how it evolved from loving kindness meditation into a daily nervous system anchor.

From gratitude and environment to health, alignment, certainty, protection, desire, and surrender, Jenna walks through the sequence she uses to intentionally train her attention. Not as superstition, but as conditioning. Through neuroplasticity, cognitive reframing, and the reticular activating system, she explains how repeated thoughts strengthen neural pathways and shift the brain out of automatic threat loops.

This isn’t about asking for things. It’s about deciding what you will focus on before your mind starts ruminating for you. It’s about orienting yourself toward your North Star instead of letting your brain run on autopilot.

If you want to participate in your life on purpose and train your brain to notice alignment, growth, and possibility, this episode will show you how to build a prayer practice that’s entirely your own.

Follow Jenna on Instagram: @jennamarilyn_

Email thoughts to: jenna.andrix@gmail.com

episodes.name: EP 37 | 12 Spiritual Ideas I Live By
episodes.description:
In this episode, Jenna Marilyn shares 12 spiritual ideas she actually lives by. Not rituals. Not aesthetics. Not things that sound profound on the internet. These are the beliefs that shape how she moves, decides, creates, and participates in her own life.

From participation without guarantees, to trusting the intelligence of the body, to choosing creation over consumption, Jenna breaks down the personal philosophies that ground her when she feels uncertain. She talks about cyclical time instead of linear pressure, detachment without disengagement, abundance as stability, and why integrity when no one is watching is the real spiritual practice.

This episode is not about floating above reality. It is about embodying what you believe inside of it. If you have ever wondered what your own spiritual ideas are, or how to live them instead of just thinking about them, this is your invitation to get clear and let it rip.

You do not need certainty. You need to participate.

Follow Jenna on Instagram: @jennamarilyn_

episodes.name: EP 36 | Not Knowing What You’re Doing (But Doing It Anyway)
episodes.description:
In this episode, Jenna Marilyn shares the core idea behind Just Jenna: not knowing what you’re doing, but doing it anyway. Not because you have it figured out. Not because you feel ready. But because life wants you to participate.

She reflects on uncertainty, being a beginner, and why waiting to feel ready keeps people stuck. You don’t need certainty about the route. You need certainty about the ground. Through self-trust, detachment from outcomes, and reconnecting to something deeper than the mind, movement becomes possible.

You don’t figure life out first. You participate in it.

episodes.name: EP 35 |Don’t Miss Your Life (Get Out of Your Head)
episodes.description:
In this episode, Jenna Marilyn talks about the quiet way people miss their own lives. Not because nothing is happening, but because they’re stuck in their heads, managing themselves, rehearsing themselves, and trying to perform the “right” way inside moments that were never meant to be controlled.

Through a conversation that sparked a revitalization, Jenna explores why anxiety is often not about the moment itself, but about fear of our own unedited expression inside it. She breaks down how living in your head creates the illusion of control while quietly pulling you out of your body, your breath, and the present moment.

This episode is a reminder that life doesn’t want to be handled. It wants to be experienced. Presence is not passive. It is an active refusal to abandon the moment and retreat into thought. When you stop trying to manage yourself and allow yourself to be here, life becomes something you actually remember.

The present moment does not need improvement. It needs your participation.

Follow Jenna on Instagram: @jennamarilyn_

Host: Jenna Marilyn

episodes.name: EP 34 |The Law of Giving: Why Sharing Changes Everything
episodes.description:
In this episode, Jenna Marilyn shares a reminder that quietly changed her entire life. Giving is not about being “good,” being selfless, or proving anything. It is about circulation. It is about keeping the channel open inside your body and inside your life.

She tells the story of a simple practice she started at 19 that made her feel like a magician in her car. Silently blessing strangers. Sending joy, peace, and goodwill with no expectation in return. Not as a belief system. As an experiment. And the result was immediate. Something softened. Something moved.

Jenna breaks down the Law of Giving through real life, nature, and systems, explaining why nothing stays alive if it does not move. Why hoarding blocks flow. And why giving and receiving are not separate actions but two ends of the same loop. She also offers simple, grounded ways to practice this in everyday life, starting with the things that cost nothing: attention, presence, listening, appreciation, and love.

episodes.name: EP 33 | When the Dream Arrives
episodes.description:
In this episode, Jenna Marilyn reflects on her podcast journey, not as a success story, but as a relationship that had to mature. What started as a long-held dream became frustrating, awkward, and imperfect once it actually arrived. And that tension taught her something important.

Jenna walks through the three evolutions of Just Jenna, from forcing it, to letting it be easy, to choosing intentional growth, and why staying with something after the fantasy dissolves is where real fulfillment begins. Along the way, she draws parallels to journaling, self-documentation, and the quiet power of capturing your thoughts across time.

episodes.name: EP 32 | The Lie of Linear Progress
episodes.description:

She breaks down why repetition, routine, and returning have been quietly devalued, and how that disconnection from natural cycles shows up as exhaustion and confusion.

Wisdom lives in staying. In returning. In tending to relationships, practices, and seasons long enough for depth to form. Meaning is not created by novelty or constant escalation. It is built through commitment, attention, and participation over time.

If you are tired of arguing with yourself, breaking promises you meant to keep, or carrying quiet shame about habits you thought you would have outgrown, this episode offers a different approach. Nothing went wrong. Nothing was dramatic. The situation unfolded, required some time and effort, and resolved the way these things usually do. What stood out was this. Before the call, during it, and after it ended, she still felt like herself. Her internal state stayed intact.

This episode is not about suppressing emotions or pretending things do not matter. It is about learning how to pause and choosing not to suffer unnecessarily when nothing is actually threatening you.

You’re not broken. You’re not behind. You’re not unmotivated.

Jenna breaks down the three ingredients every human needs to grow — the right soil (environment), the right gardeners (community), and the right season (timing). When those three line up, growth is effortless. When even one is missing, you wilt and blame the flower… instead of the conditions.

This is the code Jenna finally cracked — why Denmark bloomed her, why Chicago didn’t, and why California clicked. It wasn’t the city. It was the soil, the gardeners, and the season.

If you’ve felt stuck, sluggish, confused, or “not yourself,” this episode will shift the way you see your life. Nothing is wrong with you. Your conditions need adjusting. That’s it.

episodes.name: EP. One | CELLULAR CERTAINTY
episodes.description:
In this episode, Jenna Marilyn is talking about decisions, doubt, and the quiet certainty that lives inside your body — even when your mind is filled with fear.

In this episode, Jenna shares a moment that shifted everything: a line from The Book of Secrets by Deepak Chopra that reminded her how deeply her body knows what to do. While the mind spins in doubt, the body moves with quiet precision. It adapts. It responds. It leads — if we let it.

She opens up about her personal experience with OCD, often called “the doubting disorder,” and how indecision shaped much of her life. What helped her break free wasn’t figuring everything out — it was choosing to move, and seeing that she was supported every time.

You’ll hear about:

  • Why certainty doesn’t have to come from logic — it can come from your cells
  • The difference between mental fear and biological wisdom
  • How the universe supports you when you move with intention
  • Why you are life — and life is built to adapt
  • A redefinition of “trusting yourself” that lives deeper than thought

If you’ve ever felt stuck in fear of the “wrong” decision, or if you’ve questioned whether you can actually trust yourself — this is your reminder:

Your body already knows.

And life will meet you the moment you move.
